newsitem.title: CHINA: China Bengang Steel B share debut seen unexciting.
newsitem.headline: China Bengang Steel B share debut seen unexciting.

text.p: The usual fever surrounding China's new share issues is unlikely to grace Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd when it lists 400 million foreign currency B shares on the Shenzhen bourse on Tuesday, analysts said on Monday.

"Bengang is in China's sunset steel industry (and) I think its shares are going to hover around the offer price, if not sink," Yang Jun, a steel sector analyst with Shenzhen J&A Securities, told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

Many of China's state-controlled steel companies, saddled with debt and burdened by bloated workforces, had struggled to stay afloat since economic reforms launched in the late 1970s began dismantling a centrally planned economy, analysts said.
China has 2,000 steel factories, only 75 of which made a profit last year, they said.
Domestic steel demand grew only three percent in 1996 compared with a jump of 27 percent in 1995, analysts said.

Bengang in June completed an initial public offering priced at HK$2.38 or 2.547 yuan per share, implying a P/E ratio of 8.0 times based on fully diluted 1996 per-share earnings of 0.318 yuan under international accounting standards.
An official at the issue's international coordinator ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett in Hong Kong said the first-tranche offer was about 15 times oversubscribed.
The offer's lead domestic underwriter Shenyin & Wanguo trumpeted the listing, saying it had much head room when compared with an average P/E of 20 times for existing Shenzhen-listed B shares.
"But I see a bleak start for Bengang because the market in general is lacking strength," said Peter Ho, an analyst at PBI Securities in Shenzhen.
Shenzhen's A and B share markets have been hit by rumoured and actual government measures to stabilise the stock markets. The B index plunged 5.7 percent to 127.69 points on Monday.
Bengang's relatively large share flotation was also likely to dampen buying demand, analysts said.
Until recently, China's new shares have been greeted with jump starts on their debut days.
But Shanghai newcomer Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle Co's 900946.SS 230 million B share listing in June reversed the trend with a worse-than-expected debut.
"Bengang is in the northeastern province of Liaoning, the heart of the lumbering state heavy industries," Yang said. "I think investors are not hot on the concept."
Bengang forecast net earnings of 390 million yuan for 1997 based on international accounting standards, a Bengang official has said.
The company posted net profits of 361.5 million yuan for 1996 and 167.9 million yuan for 1995 under international standards, it said in its offering prospectus.
Bengang said it will use proceeds from the B issues to expand and renovate steel-making facilities.

Bengang has an annual hot-rolled steel production capacity of 2.2 million tonnes, with most of its products sold domestically and the rest exported to Southeast Asia, the prospectus said, adding Bengang holds 14.52 percent of China's market share.
Bengang is 57.25 percent controlled by Bengang Group Co which is among China's top 10 steel makers, it said.

Bengang Steel has 1.016 billion outstanding shares, consisting of 616 million institutional shares held by Bengang Group and 400 million B shares, according to an investment report prepared by Shenyin & Wanguo Securities.
